root_cause.text: The virtio_bt RX handler stripped the backend-supplied packet type byte and passed the remaining skb directly to `hci_recv_frame()` for HCI event/ACL/SCO/ISO packets without verifying that the payload was long enough to contain the fixed per-type HCI header, allowing zero-length or short frames to reach Bluetooth core parsing paths that read uninitialized data.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a `min_hdr` check in `virtbt_rx_handle()` for each packet type (`sizeof(struct hci_event_hdr)`, `hci_acl_hdr`, `hci_sco_hdr`, `hci_iso_hdr`) and drops the packet with `bt_dev_err_ratelimited()` if `skb->len < min_hdr`; the commit message states that previously “none of the switch cases in virtbt_rx_handle() check skb->len against the per-type minimum HCI header size before handing the frame to the core,” and specifically describes a one-byte completion reaching `hci_recv_frame()` with `skb->len` already pulled to 0.

intent_record.intent_summary: Prepare virtbt receive handling to use a minimum header length check.
intent_record.what: A new local variable declaration `size_t min_hdr;` was added at the start of `virtbt_rx_handle(struct virtio_bluetooth *vbt, struct sk_buff *skb)`. No other code in the shown hunk was modified.
intent_record.how: By introducing `min_hdr`, the function is prepared to track a minimum header length during receive handling, likely for later validation or parsing logic. In the shown hunk alone, this does not yet alter runtime behavior, but it enables header-size checks or packet validation in the function body.

intent_record.intent_summary: Validate incoming virtbt packet lengths against their expected HCI headers and drop truncated frames before handing them to the HCI layer.
intent_record.what: The switch in `virtbt_rx_handle()` was changed so each supported HCI packet type now sets a `min_hdr` size: `HCI_EVENT_PKT` uses `sizeof(struct hci_event_hdr)`, `HCI_ACLDATA_PKT` uses `sizeof(struct hci_acl_hdr)`, `HCI_SCODATA_PKT` uses `sizeof(struct hci_sco_hdr)`, and `HCI_ISODATA_PKT` uses `sizeof(struct hci_iso_hdr)`. The `default` case now returns immediately instead of breaking. After the switch, new code checks `skb->len < min_hdr`; if true, it logs a rate-limited error, frees the skb, and returns. Only if the payload is large enough does it assign `hci_skb_pkt_type(skb) = pkt_type` and call `hci_recv_frame()`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, received virtio Bluetooth packets are now validated to ensure their payload is at least large enough to contain the expected HCI header for the declared packet type. Malformed or truncated packets are rejected early with an error log instead of being passed into the HCI stack, which prevents invalid frame processing and potential downstream parsing issues.

candidates.rationale: This directly hands the received skb to the Bluetooth core without any prior length validation for the expected HCI header, which allows short or zero-length payloads to reach parsing code.

This strips the backend-supplied packet type into the skb and immediately prepares it for core processing, but the pre-fix path does not verify that the remaining payload is long enough for the packet-specific HCI header.

vuln_statements.explanation: This directly forwards the backend-provided skb to the Bluetooth core after the packet type byte has been removed, but before any validation that the remaining payload is long enough for the fixed HCI header for that packet type. That allows zero-length or truncated frames to reach core parsing paths that may read uninitialized data.

This prepares the skb for core HCI processing by setting the packet type, but in the vulnerable flow it is done without verifying that the payload remaining after stripping the type byte meets the minimum length for the corresponding HCI header.
